title: An AI chatbot for the complaints
tension: The national strategy sets an objective of adopting AI across customer services. The CPR precludes non-human agents in conversations about Consumer Complaints.

a.quote:
OBJECTIVE 4: 
ADOPT AI ACROSS CUSTOMER 
SERVICES TO IMPROVE 
LIVES AND GOVERNMENT

b.quote:
preclude the use of non-human agents by Licensees in 
conversations with Consumers regarding Consumer Complaints.

outcome: Do not use an AI chatbot in conversations with consumers about these complaints. AI elsewhere in customer service is not decided by this conflict.
honesty: The closest real tension is general against specific. The strategy objective does not mention complaints, and its discussion is largely about government.

title: An outside auditor asks for each subscriber’s usage records
tension: The Ethics guideline says external auditing should be used for critical decisions. The CPR says a Licensee must obtain prior consent before sharing Subscriber Information with third parties not directly involved in the ordered service.

a.quote:
When AI systems are used for critical decisions, external auditing of the AI systems in 
question should be used as a means to ensure meaningful standards of transparency and 
accountability are upheld.

b.quote:
Licensees must obtain a Subscriber’s prior consent 35 before sharing any 
Subscriber Information with its affiliates and/or other third parties not directly 
involved in the provision of the telecommunications services ordered by the 
Subscriber.

outcome: Must have prior consent before the auditor receives Subscriber Information, unless a person finds another ground applies. The audit itself is not ruled out: it can run on material that is not Subscriber Information.
honesty: The two texts conflict only if the audit needs Subscriber Information. The Ethics text applies only to critical decisions, and it does not address what data an auditor receives.
